Hi Maya — thanks for sending the notice. Kim / Grace — looping you in for legal/ops.

Quick answers up front so procurement can keep to the 11/20 timeline:

- Designated custodian: Grace O'Connor (ops) — grace.oconnor@redwood.com / +1 415-555-0132. Grace will coordinate any evidence transfer or access requests to our secure staging bucket.
- Retention window: We can agree to an initial 21-day staged retention for triage, with an option to extend to 45 days by mutual written request. If Synthasoft requires a hard 30-day commitment in the order form, we can discuss limited language that preserves operational flexibility (e.g., "Redwood will stage evidence for an initial 30-day period unless extended by mutual written notice").
- Defend vs reimburse: Redwood's current preference is defend-and-subrogate for third-party IP claims where we have the right to control defense. If customer insists on defend-vs-reimburse, we can offer a hybrid: Redwood defends where we have control; otherwise reimburse capped at the order-form liabilities. I'll put proposed clause language into redlines and attach them.

Kim — can you review the suggested retention language and confirm any privilege/chain-of-custody guardrails we need to add?

Action items: Grace to create an evidence intake ticket (ETA 24 hrs). Kim to provide redline text for the MSA/order form. Rafael to share draft amendment link.

On Tue, Nov 10, 2027 at 9:12 AM Synthasoft Procurement <procurement@synthasoft.com> wrote:
> Hi Rafael,
> 
> Thanks for taking my call earlier. Attached is the formal claim notice...

Thanks all — I reviewed Rafael's proposed operational stance and have a few legal recommendations to make the amendment workable for both sides and minimize downstream disputes:

1) Evidence custody & chain-of-custody: insert a short statement in the order form appendix that Redwood will maintain collected evidence in a tamper-evident staging area and will record chain-of-custody metadata (uploader, timestamp, checksum). We can provide a simple CSV export on request.

2) Retention timing: accept the 30-day initial staging window but add an explicit extension process: either party may request an additional 15-day extension with written justification; if neither party requests extension, Redwood may securely purge per our data retention procedures.

3) Privilege and privileged communications: add a carveout that communications between customer counsel and customer are preserved but that Redwood will label and quarantine privileged materials; Redwood will not waive privilege by storing materials.

4) Defense control: to avoid litigation delays, we propose the following split: Redwood will take control of defense for claims alleging infringement of third-party IP tied to Redwood-delivered model outputs where Redwood's model training or inference created the infringing output; otherwise, the customer retains control. In cases Redwood controls, Redwood will coordinate counsel and bear defense costs subject to a liability cap tied to the order form.

5) Insurer/escrow coordination: request insurer contact; if customer wants an escrow activation, we need the trigger language and escrow agent details to draft the clause.

I've drafted redline language for sections 4 and 5 (attached: redlines_v3.docx). Grace, please confirm the ticket/referral process for evidence intake and whether we can support an SFTP or secure share link for transfer.

Kimberly Park
Senior Counsel, Contracts & Privacy
Redwood Inference

Kim / Rafael / Grace — appreciate the quick turnaround and the proposed language. A few confirmations from our side:

- Synthasoft will share insurer contact and claims liaison by EOD Monday.
- We agree to the chain-of-custody metadata export (CSV) but require that Redwood retain checksum hashes for the full retention period.
- For defense control: we can accept the proposed split in principle. Our counsel (Morgan & Hale) will review the redlines_v3.docx and propose one minor change to the "control" trigger (they'll send a tracked redline).
